# Cantonese TTS

> Open text-to-speech model for Cantonese (廣東話): a 0.6B talker in GGUF that
> runs locally on the diffusion engine of the `ggk` or `gguf-core` Python
> package; `--serve` puts it behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint,
> `POST /v1/audio/speech`. Supports
> voice design (describe the voice) and voice cloning (reference recording).

Quick start:

```bash
pip install ggk        # or: pip install gguf-core  (command `gguf` instead of `ggk`)
ggk -m cantonese-1.2-0.6b-q8_0.gguf --adapter pig_cantonese_0.6b_adapter-test-f16.gguf --codec-model tts-tokenizer-12hz-q8_0.gguf --serve --port 8888
curl http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/audio/speech -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "今日天氣好好。", "voice": "A warm, low female voice."}' --output speech.mp3
```

## Docs

- [Complete guide](llms-full.txt): install, model files, server options, every request field, voice design, voice cloning, pitfalls. Self-contained; read this one.
- [Website](index.html): the same documentation for people, plus a browser playground.

## Sources

- [Model files](https://huggingface.co/cantonese-dev): the talker, the speech codec and the optional voice adapter (GGUF)
- [ggk](https://github.com/gguf-io/gk): the runtime
- [gguf-core](https://github.com/calcuis/gguf-core): the same runtime under the `gguf` command
